references.why: Uncited allusion; Segond has 'l’ouvrage de tes mains' (second person), re-personed to third person to fit the sentence.
Allusion re-personed by the author ('loved you'); Segond has 'nous a aimés'.
Allusion inside the quoted 17th-century divine, first person ('made unto me redemption'); source splits it across two paragraphs.
The quoted divine doubles 'servant of sin / slave of sin'; Segond has only 'est esclave du péché'.
Unmarked allusion recast as an imperative to the reader.
Allusion turned into a prayer (KJV 'fulfil all the good pleasure of his goodness'); Segond's wording ('desseins bienveillants de sa bonté') does not carry the author's words.
KJV 'Rest in the LORD'; Segond reads 'Garde le silence devant l’Éternel' and lacks the word 'rest' the argument turns on.
Author's paraphrase ('Take no thought for yourselves') of 'for your life'; re-worded, so not Segond verbatim.
The lilies' words applied to a baby (re-personed to the singular) in a quoted writer's line.
Allusion in the sparrow poem, re-personed ('one of us'); only 'tombe à terre' is Segond's.
Re-personed by the author ("as we have received … so we are to walk in Him"); Segond's imperative « marchez en lui » does not fit her sentence.
Loose allusion recast by the author into her own sentence ("to seat us in heavenly places with Himself").
Uncited allusion, re-personed by the author ("according to our faith" vs Segond « selon votre foi »).
Re-personed paraphrase ("He has promised to preserve our going out and coming in"); Segond has « ton départ et ton arrivée ».
Condensed paraphrase of the verse (source's own summary, 'both of man and beast'), built from Segond's vocabulary.
Allusion recast into the author's contrast (believer vs doubter); not Segond's sentence.
Segond has the past 'obtinrent des promesses'; the author applies it to believers in the present.
Segond reads 'ayant purifié leurs cœurs par la foi'; recast as a participle agreeing with 'nos cœurs'.
Re-personed ('save you'); Segond: « il peut sauver parfaitement ceux qui s’approchent de Dieu par lui ».
Re-personed to the reader; Segond: « celui qui ne croit pas Dieu le fait menteur ».
Author quotes KJV 'mixed with faith'; Segond has « elle ne trouva pas de la foi chez ceux qui l’entendirent », which lacks the image.
Allusion recast as a promise (future indicative); Segond: « Qu’il vous soit fait selon votre foi ».
Segond's words with the subjunctive « soyez » turned indicative to stand as a main clause.
Re-personed paraphrase (future tense, singular address) of Segond's wording.
Re-personed: God speaking in the first person ('à moi' for Segond's 'à Dieu'); the author's 'Yield yourselves' carries her argument.
Re-personed: God speaking in the first person, future tense; blended with Romans 6:13 in one quotation.
Past-tense, re-personed echo of the verse applied to the lady's experience.
Re-personed to the first person singular (Segond: 'vous ne vous appartenez point à vous-mêmes').
Re-personed to the first person singular (Segond: 'vous avez été rachetés à un grand prix').
The letter writes 'Christ' for Segond's 'Le Fils de Dieu'; remainder follows Segond verbatim.
KJV 'made himself of no reputation' applied to the writer; Segond 's’est dépouillé lui-même' lacks 'reputation', which the sentence turns on.
Prayer-form paraphrase ('fill you with all His fullness'), not Segond's sentence.
Re-personed exhortation (Segond: 'Marche devant ma face, et sois intègre').
Re-personed to 'vous' address and split into two sentences; wording otherwise Segond's.
Generalised paraphrase ('on' for Segond's 'tu') applied to the Spirit.
Re-personed ('notre Père') and names the sparrow; Segond has 'il n’en tombe pas un à terre sans la volonté de votre Père'.
Re-personed paraphrase (Segond: 'L’Éternel est pour moi').
Paraphrase of 'Si Dieu est pour nous, qui sera contre nous?'.
Re-personed paraphrase.
Re-personed paraphrase (Segond addresses 'tu').
Paraphrase in the present tense.
Author has 'a man’s heart' (Segond: 'le cœur du roi'); reworded around Segond’s images.
Segond’s rhetorical questions turned into statements, as the author has them.
Re-personed from 'tu' to 'il'.
Paraphrase in the author’s 'may' construction.
Author has 'those who love Him' (Segond: 'ceux qui aiment Dieu').
The chapter’s argument turns on God’s 'presence'; Segond has 'Je marcherai moi-même avec toi'.
Wrong citation in the source: the quoted words are 2 Corinthians 3:14 (not 2:14, the 'victory shout' the author means). Reference kept as given; words follow Segond 3:14 minus its stray comma.
Allusion recast as a general statement with the KJV's 'stature' (Segond: 'la durée de sa vie').
Author's own paraphrase in quotation marks ('No man can add to his stature by thinking'); re-personed, 'stature' not in Segond.
Blend: the author substitutes 'look' (cf. Isaiah 45:22) for Segond's 'Écoutez'.
Re-personed: applied to the growth ('elle') instead of the righteous man.
Author's adaptation applied to trusting souls (future tense, 'like these will be').
Allusion recast in the first person plural ("upon Him we must lay off every care"); Segond: « déchargez-vous sur lui de tous vos soucis ».
Paraphrase put in the Lord's mouth ("make your requests known to me, and I will attend to them all"); not Segond's wording.
Paraphrase ("His strength can only be made perfect in our weakness"), re-personed; Segond: « ma puissance s’accomplit dans la faiblesse ».
Inside a quotation from an unnamed old book, as an imperative; Segond: « oubliant ce qui est en arrière ».
Allusion re-personed ("the yoke He puts on you is easy. The burden He gives you is light"); Segond: « Car mon joug est doux, et mon fardeau léger ».
Allusion addressed to a single reader ("rest for your soul"); Segond: « vous trouverez du repos pour vos âmes ».
Segond's line is a rhetorical question; the author turns it into a statement about devoted servants.

Singularised and reshaped exhortation ("Yield yourself to God as one alive from the dead. May every part of you be His instrument of righteousness"); Segond: « donnez-vous vous-mêmes à Dieu, comme étant vivants de morts que vous étiez, et offrez à Dieu vos membres, comme des instruments de justice ».
KJV 'sound mind'; Segond has 'un esprit ... de sagesse' which does not fit the adjectival use, so rendered.
Allusion, re-personed (Segond: je mettrai mes lois dans leur esprit, je les écrirai dans leur cœur).
Loose allusion to Hebrews 1:1, paraphrased by the author.
Segond's « Ses voies » made explicit as « les voies de la sagesse » (the author names wisdom), quoted inside Satan's speech; otherwise Segond's wording.
Author quotes the KJV 'fall into divers temptations' to argue temptation is not sin; Segond has « épreuves », so « tentations » kept, and re-personed to « nous » (Segond wording otherwise).
Segond « Ils prennent le vol comme les aigles » put in the infinitive to fit the sentence; Segond has no 'wings'.
Allusion to 'Sanctifiez-vous pour demain', re-personed into the third person infinitive.
Paraphrase ('making God a liar'); Segond has 'le fait menteur', recast around the author's phrase.
Allusion re-personed to the woman in the story (Segond: 'plus que vainqueurs par celui qui nous a aimés').
KJV Ps 19:13 = Segond 19:14. The author prays against 'presumptuous sins'; Segond reads 'des orgueilleux' (proud people), so the object is rendered as sins to keep her point; the rest follows Segond.
Indirect allusion; the author says 'save' where Segond has 'appeler' (call).
Allusion ('flesh-pots of Egypt'); Segond's 'pots de viande' kept but the phrase is recast.
Allusion re-personed to second person plural (Segond: 'qu’il renonce à lui-même, qu’il se charge de sa croix').
Narrative allusion in past tense following the KJV 'lift up a standard', which Segond does not have ('L’esprit de l’Éternel le mettra en fuite').
Allusion re-personed to 'vous' (Segond: 'Va, et toi, fais de même').
Allusion re-personed and put in the present ('vous aime'); Segond: 'plus que vainqueurs par celui qui nous a aimés'.
Unquoted allusion, re-personed (vous→nous) and 'praises' kept for the author's wording; Segond has « les vertus ».
Allusion re-personed to 'we'; Segond has 'Prenez mon joug sur vous... vous trouverez du repos'.
KJV-shaped wording ('as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride') applied to the reader; Segond words it differently ('comme la fiancée fait la joie de son fiancé').
Re-personed allusion (they may... cast out your name as evil).
Paraphrase blended into the Luke 6:23 quotation (cf. 1 Peter 4:13); not Segond's wording.
KJV-shaped allusion ('see of the travail of his soul, and be satisfied') applied in present tense to the believer; Segond's phrasing differs.
Re-personed from 'we' to 'they'.
The author writes "His nature"; Segond has "la nature divine" — kept her wording on Segond's "participants de".
Allusion re-personed to the reader ("you will not revile again"); Segond: "injurié, ne rendait point d’injures".
Re-personed, blended allusion (KJV "despitefully use you"); not Segond's sentence.
Re-personed to the believer ("his body … who is in him, who is of God"); Segond: "votre corps … qui est en vous, que vous avez reçu de Dieu".
Re-personed allusion ("your body continually bearing the dying of the Lord Jesus"); Segond: "portant toujours avec nous dans notre corps la mort de Jésus".
Re-personed to the reader; Segond: "la vie de Jésus soit aussi manifestée dans notre chair mortelle".

Segond opens with « Car » and the indicative future; the author's whole argument turns on the verse's concessive « Although », so the verse is recast concessively (« Quoique… ») keeping Segond's vocabulary.
Segond reads « je n’ai rien à espérer », the opposite of the author's point (hope in God in trial); rendered from her English.
Segond has « au milieu de vous »; the author's whole argument rests on 'within you' (an interior kingdom), so « au-dedans de vous » is kept (both occurrences, paragraphs 1 and 3).
Allusion, reworded in indirect speech using Segond's vocabulary.
Paraphrased and re-personed allusion (dragons and adders trodden under foot); not Segond's wording.
Reordered infinitive paraphrase of the verses, built from Segond's vocabulary.
The author has 'servant of all' (Mark 10:44 wording) where Segond's Matthew 20:27 has 'votre esclave'; her wording kept.
Uncited allusion; the author says 'all other kingdoms' where Segond has 'tous ces royaumes-là'.
The author's point is suffering (KJV 'if we suffer'); Segond has 'si nous persévérons'.
The author's re-personed prayer built on Elisha's (« ouvre ses yeux, pour qu’il voie »); plural form is hers.
Allusion to KJV 'ride prosperously' (Ps 45:4 KJV = Segond 45:5 « Sois vainqueur, monte sur ton char »); re-personed to the plural 'we'.
Re-personed from Segond « la multitude de mes chars ».
Re-personed from Segond « descendent en Égypte pour avoir du secours ».
Segond lacks 'alone'; the author's argument ('He only') rests on it, so « seul » is added to Segond's wording.
Segond « c’est lui qui est mon rocher » lacks 'only'; the author's 'He only' argument depends on it.
Allusion to KJV Ps 40:2 'established my goings' (Segond 40:3 « Il a affermi mes pas »), re-personed as 'our goings are established'.
Allusion ('the arms of God'); Segond has « ses bras éternels ».
The author's personal prayer modelled on Elisha's; re-personed.
Re-tensed from Segond « celui qui s’avance dans les cieux » (the author's 'ride upon the heavens').
The author's recurring phrase; Segond reads « chars de l’Éternel ».
Re-personed by the author ("acknowledge God in all our ways"); Segond: « Reconnais-le dans toutes tes voies ».

The author's argument (mothers giving sleep to their beloved children) depends on the KJV sense "he giveth his beloved sleep"; Segond reads « Il en donne autant à ses bien-aimés pendant leur sommeil ».
Allusion ('taking up His home'); Segond « J’établirai ma demeure au milieu de vous » recast in the past tense and third person.
Allusion; Segond « os de mes os et chair de ma chair » re-personed to « nos ».
Segond reads « C’est toi qui as formé mes reins »; the author's point (He is not only with us but within us) rests on the KJV 'possessed my reins', so that sense is kept, re-personed.
Segond « Même les ténèbres ne sont pas obscures pour toi » re-personed to the third person.
Segond « Tu sais quand je m’assieds et quand je me lève » re-personed (both occurrences).

The author follows the KJV 'compassest my path and my lying down' and builds on path/lying down (seats, beds); Segond « Tu sais quand je marche et quand je me couche » lacks 'path', so rendered and re-personed (both occurrences).
The author's argument plays on KJV 'beset' (as one is beset by unwelcome people); Segond's « Tu m’entoures » cannot carry that, so « assiéger » is used (also the sense of the Hebrew).
The author follows the KJV 'in thy book all my members were written'; Segond has « Les jours », so her word « membres » is kept.
Segond « nous sommes son ouvrage »; « son » made explicit as « de Dieu ».
Segond « un vase d’honneur » pluralised to match 'we'.
Segond « sanctifié, utile à son maître, propre à toute bonne œuvre » pluralised and « Maître » as the author's 'the Master'.

Segond reads « me semblent impénétrables »; the author's point is that the Psalmist calls God's thoughts 'precious' (hence kind and loving), so « précieuses » is kept; second half is Segond verbatim. Same wording at both occurrences.
Allusion ('He hears the young lions when they cry'); Segond « Les lionceaux rugissent après la proie » recast as a relative clause.
Paraphrase; Segond « il n’en tombe pas un à terre sans la volonté de votre Père ».
The author's 'dwell at ease' (KJV Ps 25:13); Segond « Son âme reposera dans le bonheur » recast as an infinitive.
